architectureNote: Unlike USS and USS One, this file has NO local Color/Figma-Color variable collections at all (getLocalVariableCollectionsAsync returns only Space + Radius). All color is delivered instead through 529 local PAINT STYLES (legacy Figma styles, not variables) — consistent with this file's role as a shared 'Extension Library' that layers additional styles on top of a consumed/published core, rather than owning canonical token variables itself.

paintStyleTotals.duplicationNote: All 195 'extra' objects live under the 'Light mode/' folder: every one of its 65 distinct semantic token names (Background/Surface/Border/Text/Links/Text interactive/Icons/Feedback/Focus/Buttons) exists as exactly 4 separate PaintStyle objects with identical names AND identical resolved hex values but different style IDs/keys. 'Dark mode' and all base-palette/accent folders have clean 1x copies. This looks like a library-hygiene artifact from repeated imports/merges rather than an intentional design choice — flagged as a cleanup opportunity.

semanticTokens.note: 65 distinct semantic tokens (one fewer than USS One's 66 — missing 'Background 4'). Category counts below reflect DISTINCT names only, with duplicates already collapsed out.

categories.note: Sum = 65 (Light mode). Dark mode mirrors this 1:1 plus 2 extra 'Elevation (reemplazo a sombra)' tokens = 67 total dark-mode styles.

sampleResolvedValues.note: Sampled tokens confirmed to resolve to the SAME hex values as USS/USS One — this Extension Library shares the same core brand palette, it just packages it differently (styles vs variables, with duplication).

basePalettes.note: 85 distinct base-palette swatches under '_Base/' (vs 92 in USS One) — all Neutral/Primary/Secondary-Verde/Info/Success/Warning/Error ramps confirmed IDENTICAL hex values to USS One. The difference is structural: this file renames the second (blue-gray) ramp '_Base/Terciary' instead of '_Base/Secondary', AND gives 'Terciary' a completely different, unrelated PURPLE ramp — while the Facultad/USS accent tokens below still resolve to the ORIGINAL blue-gray hex values via hardcoded solid colors (no alias to any local base group could be found).

Terciary (NEW — purple ramp, unrelated t.note: 90 and 100 resolve to the identical hex (#402851) — likely an unfinished/duplicated ramp step.

basePalettes.otherRamps: Secondary - Verde, Info, Success, Warning, Error — 10 steps each, confirmed identical to USS One's basePalettes (see USS One Design System Inventory/tokens/colors.json for full values).

accentTheming.note: The Facultad/USS/Tono-Exito/Tono-Alerta/Tono-Error accent system from USS One is present here too, as flat paint styles (not aliased variables), with IDENTICAL resolved hex values. New here: a 'text/facultad/on-light' subgroup and 'elevacion/on-dark' tokens with a DIFFERENT dark-elevation color (#121c27) than USS One's (#1d2633).

elevacion/on-dark.note: Flat, identical across all 4 levels — differs from USS One's #1d2633.

vsUSSOne: Same brand color values throughout, but delivered via 529 legacy paint styles (334 distinct) instead of a 343-variable 'Color' collection — no local color VARIABLES exist in this file at all. Introduces a heavy duplication artifact (4x copies of every Light-mode semantic style) and a new unrelated purple 'Terciary' base ramp not seen in USS One.
